entries.name: QUICKBOOKS_CLIENT_ID
entries.description: Client ID of the KaratOS app on the Intuit Developer portal, used with the client secret to refresh QuickBooks access tokens.
howToGet: On developer.intuit.com, open the app under My Hub > App dashboard, then Keys and credentials. Use the Development keys with the sandbox company and the Production keys with the client's company.
Copy the Client ID straight into the host's secret store.

entries.name: QUICKBOOKS_CLIENT_SECRET
entries.description: Client secret of the Intuit app. It refreshes access tokens and is the key the instance encrypts its stored refresh token with, so rotating it means reconnecting QuickBooks.
howToGet: In the same Keys and credentials page, copy the Client Secret straight into the host's secret store.
After rotating it, reconnect the company and set a new QUICKBOOKS_REFRESH_TOKEN, because the stored token can no longer be decrypted.

entries.name: QUICKBOOKS_REALM_ID
entries.description: The QuickBooks company's realm ID, shown as Company ID. Not a secret, but it names the client's books.
howToGet: The realmId comes back with the authorization code when the company is connected.
In QuickBooks it is under Settings > Account and settings > Billing and subscription, as Company ID.

entries.name: QUICKBOOKS_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from connecting the company. Intuit rotates it about daily, so after the first sync the instance keeps the newest one encrypted in its database and this value only seeds it. Replacing it here (after reconnecting) takes over from the stored one.
howToGet: Have a QuickBooks admin connect the company to the KaratOS app with the com.intuit.quickbooks.accounting scope, for example through Intuit's OAuth 2.0 Playground with the app's own keys.
Copy the refresh token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.
Intuit has no read-only accounting scope; the connector only sends GET requests, and its writes stay behind the write gate.

entries.name: QUICKBOOKS_ENVIRONMENT
entries.description: Which QuickBooks API the company is on: sandbox for an Intuit developer sandbox company, production for a real one. There is no default, so a sandbox setting can't reach a client's books by accident and the other way round.
howToGet: Use sandbox with Development keys and production with Production keys.

entries.name: QUICKBOOKS_WEBHOOK_VERIFIER_TOKEN
entries.description: Verifier token for QuickBooks webhooks, which signs each delivery (intuit-signature). Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: On the app's Webhooks page on developer.intuit.com, copy the Verifier Token straight into the host's secret store.
